buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer uploaded ATC document Click here to view the file. 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Description: High End Computer WorkStation 1) Pre-Qualification Criteria: 1a) Experience: Bidder shall submit at least one purchase order copy for supply of workstation w ith minimum 32 GB RAM in the last 5 years from the date of enquiry. 1b) Relaxation of Norms for Start-ups: The condition of Prior Turnover and prior experience is relaxed for all start-ups whether Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs) or otherwise subject to meeting of quality and technical specifications in accordance with the relevant provision of GFR,2005 and other DOE-PPD notifications for relaxation norms for start-ups issued from time to time. 2) Payment term: 100% basic payment shall be made within stipulated days as mentioned belo w from the date of successful installation & commissioning of material at BHEL Corporate R&D, Hy derabad, against submission of GST compliant Invoice and submission of Performance Bank Guara ntee (PBG) by supplier in the prescribed format. Type of bidder: A. For Micro & Small enterprises (MSEs) payment will be made within 45 days B. For Medium Enterprises will be made within 60 days C. Non MSMEs will be made within 90 days However, GST Portion of Invoice shall be released only upon: i) Vendor declaring the Invoice in their GSTR-1. ii) Receipt of Goods and Tax Invoice by BHEL. iii) Confirmation of Payment of GST thereon by vendor on GSTN.

Note: “Payment Timelines” mentioned in the GeM Bid document shall be ignored and the Paymen t term shall be as per this clause. 3) Invoice Settlement for MSME Suppliers: In respect of procurement of goods or services fro m Micro, Small and Medium enterprises (MSMEs), the settlement of invoice shall be only through T ReDS platforms authorised by the Reserve Bank of India. Presently BHEL Corp. R&D is registered with the following TReDS platforms: RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart. Such MSME suppliers to select their preferred TReDS platform before award of contract. They also will have the option to change the TReDS platform from the drop-down menu on Suvidh a portal of BHEL, at the time of invoice submission. The routing of invoices through the TReDS platform shall not be construed as mandating discounti ng of such invoices and the MSME suppliers shall have the option to avail or not avail financing or discounting of its receivables on the TReDS platform. In case discounting is not availed by MSME supplier on TReDS, the trade receivables will be pa id through TReDS as per the payment timelines indicated in the contract. 4) Invoice registration and documents upload in SUVIDHA portal by suppliers: Irrespective of the value of the invoice amount, the bidder/vendor should necessarily upload the d espatch & invoice details on BHEL SUVIDHA portal at https://suvidha.bhel.in/suvidha/, prior to desp atch. All documents as per PO checklist, along with additional documents (if any), must be uploade d on the portal. It is mandatory that tax invoices with a net amount (including taxes) exceeding Rs five lakhs uploaded on the portal are digitally signed using a Class 3 Digital Signature Certificate ( DSC) issued by a licensed Certifying Authority. Submission of invoice document in hard copy is all owed for invoices with a net amount (including taxes) equal to and upto Rs five lakhs, in case they were not digitally signed and uploaded on the portal. The material will not be accepted inside BHE L in absence of the above. 5) Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG): PBG of 10% of total order value is to be submitted by the successful vendor and shall be kept valid up to guarantee period. Expiry of claim period may b e kept 3-6 months after validity date. PBG shall be from one of the Consortium banks of BHEL or fr om a reputed bank and confirmed by any Consortium bank of BHEL. The offers of the suppliers not accepting to this clause will be rejected. Pro-forma of Performance Bank Guarantee is attached in ATC document Annexure-D. Note: “ePBG Detail” mentioned in the GeM Bid document shall be ignored and the PBG requireme nt shall be as per this clause. 6) Modes of Performance security/ PBG deposit: PBG/ Performance security may be furnishe d in the following forms: (i) Local cheques of Scheduled Banks (subject to realization) / Pay Order/ Demand Draft / Electroni c Fund Transfer in favor of BHEL. (ii) Bank Guarantee from Scheduled Banks / Public Financial Institutions as defined in the Compani es Act. The Bank Guarantee format should have the approval of BHEL. (iii) Fixed Deposit Receipt issued by Scheduled Banks / Public Financial Institutions as defined in th e Companies Act (FDR should be in the name of the Contractor, a/c BHEL). (iv) Securities available from Indian Post offices such as National Savings Certificates, Kisan Vikas Patras etc. (held in the name of Contractor furnishing the security and duly endorsed/ hypothecate

d/ pledged, as applicable, in favor of BHEL). (v) Insurance Surety Bond. (Note 1: BHEL will not be liable or responsible in any manner for the collection of interest or renew al of the documents or in any other matter connected therewith) Note 2: Procedure to be followed in case FD is submitted for Performance Security a) Fixed Deposit should be pledged in favour of “BHEL Corporate R&D, Hyderabad”. b) The fixed deposit should be endorsed by the bidder in the name of company, at the backside b y stating that “I/We are endorsing this FD in favour of BHEL Corporate R&D, Hyderabad” (the e ndorsement should be duly signed by the depositor/s on revenue stamp). c) The FD should be accompanied with authority letter from the bidder, authorizing BHEL Corporat e R&D, Hyderabad for unconditional encashment of FD as per the format given in Annexure E-1 enclosed with this tender document. d) The FD should be accompanied with CC copy of authority letter from the bidder, addressed to Branch Manager of the FD issuing bank, authorizing BHEL Corporate R&D, Hyderabad for uncon ditional encashment of FD as per the format given in Annexure E-2 enclosed with this tender do cument. e) The FD should be accompanied with letter from the Branch Manager of the FD issuing bank, co nfirming lien in favour of BHEL Corporate R&D, Hyderabad & unconditional encashment of FD a s per the format given in Annexure E-3 enclosed with this tender document. 7) Interest for delayed submission of performance security (PBG): PBG of 10% of total ord er value is to be submitted by the successful vendor within 15 days from the date of successful ins tallation & commissioning of material at BHEL Corporate R&D. Bidder agrees to submit performanc e security required for execution of the contract within the time period mentioned. In case of dela y in submission of performance security, enhanced performance security which would include inte rest (Repo rate + 4%) for the delayed period, shall be submitted by the bidder. Further, if perform ance security is not submitted till such time the bill becomes due, the amount of performance sec urity due shall be recovered as per terms defined in NIT/contract, from the bills along with due int erest. 8) SFMS Confirmation of Bank Guarantees (BGs) : Vendor/Contractor/Bidder to ensure that is suance of Bank Guarantee shall be confirmed by the issuing Bank directly to the Owner mandatori ly through Structured Financial Messaging System (SFMS), as it provides an RBI supported Integrat ed Platform for Bank Guarantee Verification. SBI Bank has been designated as BHEL Corporate R&D’s Bank for receiving SFMS messages for BG s issued in favour of BHEL Corporate R&D.BG shall only be obtained from Banks and Branches whi ch are live on SFMS platform i.e. which have infrastructure to issue SFMS confirmation message al ong with the BG. For SFMS, BHEL Corporate R&D Bank Details / other information are as follows: SBI Bank, HAL campus Branch, Balanagar, Hyderabad. IFSC Code: SBIN0001676. Vendor/Contractor/Bidder to take a print out of SFMS confirmation message from the BG issuing b ank branch and attach copy of same along with the hardcopy of BG while submitting the same to BHEL Corporate R&D. Same process has to be followed for any verification of BG amendment as w

ell. 9) Compliance on restrictions under Rule 144 (XI) of the GFR: Submit the Annexure - A whi ch is attached in ATC document. 10) Compliance on Treatment of cases regarding conflict of interest: Submit the Annexur e - B which is attached in ATC document. 11) Compliance on Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) order: Submit the A nnexure-C which is attached in ATC document. 12) Technical Specification: Bidder shall submit compliance on attached BHEL Technical specifi cation uploaded in Buyer Specification Document 13) Terms of Delivery: FOR BHEL R&D, Hyderabad. 14) Vendor has to submit this GeM bid document duly signed and stamped on all pages. By submi tting singed Gem bid document it affirms that vendor has accepted to all terms and conditions me ntioned in this bid such as payment terms, delivery period, Terms of Delivery, Breach of contract, Remedies and Termination, Invoice registration and documents upload in SUVIDHA portal by suppl iers etc. 15) Vendor has to quote price(s) inclusive of GST, Transportation/Insurance, Loading/Unloading charges. Insurance, loading/unloading from vendor site to BHEL R&D, Hyderabad will be in vendor scope only. 16) Safety and statutory requirement: The contractor / vendor shall ensure all safety and stat utory requirement related to its staff. 17) Banned firms: The offers of the bidders who are under suspension as also the offers of the bi dders, who engage the services of the banned firms / principal / agents, shall be rejected. The list of banned firms is available on BHEL web site https://www.bhel.com/supplier-registration 18) Breach of contract, Remedies and Termination: In case of breach of contract, wherever the value of security instruments like performance bank g uarantee available with BHEL against the said contract is atleast 10% of the contract value, the sa me be encashed. In case the value of the security instruments available is less than 10% of the co ntract value, the balance amount be recovered from other financial remedies (i.e. available bills of the contractor, retention amount, etc. with BHEL) or legal remedies be pursued. Further, levy of liq uidated damages, debarment, termination, de-scoping, short-closure, etc., shall be applied as per provisions of the contract. 19) Grievance Redressal Mechanism: To promote transparency and ensure fair treatment of a ll bidders, a structured Grievance Redressal Mechanism is in place to address any concerns or issu es arising during the tendering process or in subsequent business dealings with the company. Suppliers/Contractors are requested to follow the below escalation process for grievance resolutio n: 1) First Level: Any grievance should initially be addressed to the designated Dealing Officer, whos e contact details are provided in the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT)/Contract. 2) Second Level: If the issue remains unresolved, it may be escalated by lodging a formal grievanc e through the SUVIDHA Portal: https://suvidha.bhel.in/suvidha/. Responses will be provided in acco rdance with the defined escalation matrix.”
